## Stable outcome

Let a governed CyberAlchemy Context request and consume a challengeable ontology projection calculated deterministically from canonical per-node and per-relation events at one exact event cut, while preserving authority boundaries and rejecting stale, mixed, missing, or unverifiable cuts.

## Epoch contribution

Make the existing event-calculated ontology projection capability consumable through an isolated, versioned public adapter surface bound to the tested Governance-to-Ontology-Lifecycle v2 Context Map, without changing admitted runtime bytes or ontology truth.

## Input contracts

- one exact consistent event cut from canonical per-subject semantic and governance histories
- one immutable Governance Decision Evidence Envelope joined to the exact semantic event identity, digest, and cursor
- one context selector naming the admitted Governance and Ontology Lifecycle v2 endpoints
- the tested additive Context Map/v2 candidate at one exact digest

## Output contracts

- one deterministic Ontology Lifecycle projection exposed through a public versioned adapter symbol
- exact event, cursor, context, map, and adapter-version traceability
- typed failure for stale governance join, mixed cut, missing endpoint, map mismatch, or unverifiable evidence
- no authority, admission, or canonical replay-source effect

## Promised behaviors

- Preserve canonical event histories as the only replay source.
- Calculate node and relation state at one exact consistent cut.
- Translate immutable Governance decision evidence downstream without transferring authority.
- Resolve the exact v2 Context Map endpoints and reject any v1/v2 mixture.
- Expose adapters only from an isolated successor crate while leaving admitted runtime bytes unchanged.
- Return deterministic projections and typed failures through a public testable interface.

## Product-test obligations

- public consumers can import both versioned adapter modules from the isolated candidate crate
- the full admitted predecessor replay and context-binding suite remains green
- v2 endpoint and map identity checks reject wrong-version and reverse-direction mutations
- two identical event histories and selectors produce byte-identical projections
- admitted runtime and v1 map digests remain unchanged
- rollback rehearsal restores every selected preimage digest before cutover eligibility

## Exclusions

- making a Context, map, projection, snapshot, index, graph, or system ontology a canonical event source
- changing the stable Product Capability identity or outcome
- changing or replacing the admitted D65-S8 runtime during prototype construction
- creating a reverse Ontology-Lifecycle-to-Governance authority dependency
- transferring Governance authority through the decision evidence envelope
- performing migration, cutover, publication, release, deployment, credential use, destructive action, or another external effect

## Challenge route

Challenge the stable capability outcome through the CyberAlchemy product owner; challenge this epoch contribution through the Ontology Lifecycle Project and product-test owners. Any change to the stable outcome requires a successor Product Capability rather than a contribution rewrite.

## Claim ceiling

A D65-S2 Product Capability contribution prototype that preserves the existing capability identity and outcome while defining a testable isolated v2 adapter-export objective. It does not approve or adopt the capability, prove implementation or conformance, admit or activate the v2 map, export an adapter, authorize cutover, publish, release, deploy, or create an external effect.
